description: Mega Image receipt: a small low-quality screenshot with a watermark behind the text. Noisy Tesseract output, plus the clean text a Live Text / Lens copy would give.
notes: No store name is printed. The chain cue is the card-slip line `TERMINAL ... COMERCIANT MEGA...` (its digits are masked). Each item is `name price`, followed by its EAN on the next line; the EANs print 12 digits (truncated), kept as printed. No VAT, quantity or payment lines are printed above the slip, so none are in the ground truth.

source.ocr-text.json is tesseract.js 7 (ron+eng) on a preprocessed copy of the 420x437 screenshot (green channel, 3x Lanczos upscale, normalised, threshold 150), confidence 75. The run on the unprocessed image is unreadable (confidence 29) and is not included.

Misreads in source.ocr-text.json: line 0 price `17,85` (printed 17,89); line 1 `C2JU CRUDE 20CG` (CAJU CRUDE 200G) and EAN `853042107579` (859042107579); line 4 `EMM:` (EMMA); EAN `853042107549` (859042107549); line 6 `LCR 3S` and price `18,93` (10R 3S, 19,99); EAN `534506503482` (594906503482); date label `DAT?`.
source.pasted-text.json is the same text with those misreads corrected from the printed receipt.

expected.json is the truth. expected.ocr-text.json reads the OCR text literally: nothing in it can be repaired by arithmetic, so the lines keep their misreads and carry SUM_MISMATCH (they add up to 64,76 against a printed total of 65,86).
`CARE HARTIE 10R 3S` has no pack parsePackSize can read; the 10 rolls (2,00 lei per roll, plan section 7) come from the catalog alias default pack.
The number under TOTAL and the whole card slip (except the merchant-code letters and the date/time line) are masked: letters x, digits 0.
